value: 35g is DEFERRED: no run, schedule or pre-registration until LR-1 explicit rungs evaluated under this signature with a draft decision record; LR-2 a documented held-out failure against a failure criterion registered in advance; LR-3 a non-circular supervised target; LR-4 licence-cleared training data (recipes: training_allowed = YES only); LR-5 a signed addendum 35.0-A1 + H4/H3 approval + matched-capacity controls; learned = parameters fit to a task objective, any pretrained encoder (even frozen), any KG/graph or dimensionality-reduced embedding (PCA/SVD/LSA/autoencoder/word2vec/node2vec); explicit-feature supervised classifiers are baselines
rationale: R-16: learned rungs stay DEFERRED until explicit rungs are evaluated; SSOT s133.3 "E7 may not be reported without E0-E3".

value: the 222-character hex fingerprint string is decoded with a pinned bit order and payload/padding convention, verified in a unit test on >= 3 published PubChem CIDs before any use; convention: bits MSB-first, bit k = (byte[k // 8] >> (7 - k % 8)) & 1 for k < 881; assert length 222 hex characters and that the 7 pad bits are all 0 for every row; never use int()/bin() without zero-padding to 888 bits; failing the test blocks every E1 and tau881-based arm
rationale: Stored string length (222 hex = 888 bits) differs from the 881-bit definition; the convention must be proven, not assumed. [R3: reviewer check found 222 hex characters for all 1726 rows and 0 non-zero pad bits, consistent with 881 + 7 pad bits without a length prefix.]

value: PRESENCE profiles (SRC-000451) are analysis-only / DERIVED_ONLY; no release of per-ingredient profiles or derived scores; every output carries a licence_scope field; any public table needs an H2 decision; all outputs derived from SRC-000451 are local-only: they are written under the git-ignored features/step35/ (not under ledgers/representation/ or registry/splits/, which are not ignored), the ignore status is re-checked with git check-ignore before the first output is written, and only a sha256 manifest is tracked; .gitignore is not edited

value: tau_cluster = the 99th percentile of tau881 (PubChem-881 Tanimoto) over 20000 random molecule pairs drawn with a fixed recorded seed from the 1726 molecules, clipped to [0.60, 0.85]; sensitivity grid tau_cluster - 0.05 and + 0.05; computed before any label join; no label, score, fold size or model output may enter; value and seed written into the hashed split manifest; DEGENERATE rule (largest S-mol-cc component > 30% of scored molecules) unchanged and tau_cluster is never retuned
rationale: Review B 35-9: a fixed 0.60 is a round number not anchored to the fingerprint's own distribution, and substructure-key Tanimoto runs high for small flavour molecules, so leader clustering at 1 - 0.60 is likely to chain into a DEGENERATE component. The procedure, not the value, is registered; it reads no label, so it is not tuning (R-08 spirit). 20000 pairs and the 99th percentile are proposals.

quantity: Taste-label negatives, source-database confound control, DEPRECATED-edge audit
value: (a) for a scored class c: positives = molecules with an ACTIVE edge mapped to c; negatives = only molecules with an explicit negative for c (for example a Non-bitter string) or from a source database that assays c per a reviewed assay-coverage table (database x class: ASSAYED / NOT_ASSAYED / UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN treated as NOT_ASSAYED); every other molecule is excluded from the task for c, never a negative; a class additionally needs >= 30 confirmed-negative molecules else NEED_DATA; (b) NC35-14 source-database-only baseline and per-source-stratified AUPRC are reported next to PE-35a; the class result is SOURCE_DB_CONFOUNDED (no headline) when the lower 95% paired cluster-bootstrap bound of (strongest explicit arm minus NC35-14) is not above the THR-35P-08 AUPRC margin 0.02; (c) before signature a human establishes the reason of the 204 DEPRECATED edges and the counts by reason are recorded
rationale: Review B 35-3: one-vs-rest negatives were molecules lacking an edge (positive-unlabelled data); bittersweet curates only bitter/sweet and ChemTastesDB more classes, so the source database predicts label availability and chemotype and a classifier can score by recognising the database. 71% of ACTIVE edges are from one AGPL-3.0 source. The ledger records one reason string for all 204 DEPRECATED edges (no longer derived). The 0.02 margin is reused from THR-35P-08, the 30-negative floor is a proposal.

value: Monte-Carlo p = (b + 1) / (B + 1); for a BH family of m tests B >= max(1000, ceil(20 * m / q)) with q = 0.05 per null model (M0, MF, MC, MFC, Curveball); m (motifs passing the support rule) is fixed before any null is drawn and the maximum compute budget is recorded in the run manifest before the run; if max(1000, ceil(20 * m / q)) exceeds the budget the family uses the exact/hypergeometric or Curveball-calibrated z p-value for the BH step (label Z_CALIBRATED) with Curveball draws (>= 1000) for calibration only; the option is chosen from m and the budget, never from observed p-values; the 1000 randomisations of THR-35P-13 remain a calibration count for null percentiles
rationale: Review B 35-7: with 1000 draws the smallest Monte-Carlo p is 1/1001, so BH at q = 0.05 can reject only when p <= 0.05 * k / m; for m in the hundreds the gate fails mechanically whatever the signal, inviting a post-hoc rise of the draw count. The floor of 1000 draws of the earlier text is kept (B is never below it), so the rule only adds draws; registering it before any run strengthens the gate (no weakening).

quantity: BAN-35-1: Recipe1M/FlavorGraph-derived inputs banned from all arms
value: no arm, comparator, mapping heuristic, tie-breaker or prior may use FlavorGraph ingredient-ingredient edges, FlavorGraph node embeddings, KGE ING_CO_OCCURS edges of either origin (SRC-000451 NPMI or corpus-mined) or any Recipe1M-derived statistic; only IMAP PRESENCE ingredient -> compound rows may enter chemistry arms; the evaluation entry point lints every arm's input manifest against this list (planted-arm control NC35-17) and refuses to run on a violation
rationale: Review B 35-2: FlavorGraph edges and embeddings are built from Recipe1M, whose recipes may overlap the TEST partition of S-rec-grp, so the earlier ban on KGE edges 'as relevance' left comparator arms, mapping heuristics and co-occurrence priors open to leakage; the 298-ingredient universe was itself selected by FlavorGraph's Recipe1M frequency (selection effect, section 16).

value: molecule records whose canonical SMILES contain a dot (15 of 1726) are flagged MULTI_COMPONENT, excluded from every scored set and listed in the split manifest until a structure toolkit is approved; afterwards each is grouped with the InChIKey block of its largest organic fragment computed with the pinned toolkit; planted salt-twin control NC35-15 must be flagged by the split auditor; the phrase 'salt-blind' is not used for 14-character blocks
rationale: Review B 35-4: the first InChIKey block hashes the connectivity of all components, so a salt or mixture does not share a block with its parent and salt twins could straddle train and test under S-mol-conn; fragment standardisation needs a toolkit (rdkit absent).

quantity: Cold-start ingredient split and secondary endpoint PE-35b-cold
value: S-ing-cold: a seeded random 20% of the 298 profiled ingredients, stratified by profile-size quartile (not by frequency), are cold-start entities and every recipe containing one is removed from the train partition; query = cold entity with >= 3 relevant partners, partner relevant if it co-occurs with the query in >= 2 test-partition recipes with NPMI >= 0 computed inside the test partition; PE-35b-cold (secondary) = MAP@10 of IDF-overlap minus the better of frequency-only and cardinality-only on these queries, with a breakdown by test-partition frequency tertile; co-occurrence-from-train has no information on cold queries
rationale: Review B 35-8: TASK-ING-A queries are frequent ingredients, where popularity comparators are strongest and chemistry least needed; cold-start is the setting in which chemistry could matter and was untested. 20%, 3 partners and 2 co-occurrences are proposals.

value: PE-35d = macro-F1 of a C1-fingerprint classifier on the source-disjoint split S-cui-src minus the prevalence baseline, for classes meeting THR-35P-22; the source-identity-only baseline is not subtracted on S-cui-src (test sources are unseen in training, the baseline collapses to the prior) and is reported on the within-source split S-rec-grp (C1 classifier minus source-identity-only); the THR-35P-26 drop ratio is the cuisine = source confound test
rationale: Review B 35-5: subtracting a source-identity baseline on a source-disjoint split is vacuous and could never reveal the cuisine = source confound it is meant to catch.

quantity: Recipe split group-disjointness rules (S-rec-src, S-rec-grp strata)
value: S-rec-src: the test side excludes every recipe whose split group has a member in a training source (cross-source duplicates; count removed reported; planted control NC35-16); S-rec-grp: the stratum of a group = the source family of its lowest recipe_id member (deterministic); multi-source groups are counted and reported
rationale: Review B 35-6: source-disjoint is not group-disjoint when the same recipe appears on BBC and Food.com (07I-C cross_source), and source stratification is undefined for groups spanning sources.

value: ingredients with identical PRESENCE sets are counted and reported; merged into one cluster in S-ing-clu and treated as a single profile in the nulls and in TASK-ING-A query sets
rationale: Review B 35-11: FlavorDB-derived profiles often copy one generic compound list to related entities; identical sets score 1 for CHEMICAL and STRUCTURAL, distort the Curveball null and create near-duplicate queries.
